title: Lighting Controls Design Basics
summary: The core building blocks of a lighting controls design: sensing, zoning, dimming, and code-driven strategies.

blocks.content: Most lighting controls designs combine four strategies: occupancy/vacancy sensing, daylight harvesting, scheduling, and manual/task tuning. Energy codes usually require several of these in combination.
Occupancy sensing turns lights ON and OFF based on presence; vacancy sensing only turns them OFF automatically (manual-on). Codes often mandate vacancy (manual-on) in specific space types.
A control zone is a group of fixtures that respond together. Finer zoning gives more energy savings and flexibility but adds devices and cost.
Match zoning to how a space is actually used: perimeter (daylight) zones separate from interior zones, and private offices controlled individually.
Daylight zones should be parallel to the window wall so photocells dim only the fixtures that actually receive daylight.
Common dimming protocols include 0-10V (simple analog), DALI (digital, addressable per-fixture), and phase control (legacy).
0-10V and DALI are not interchangeable at the driver — confirm the fixture driver matches the control protocol the design specifies.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between occupancy and vacancy sensing?

choices.text: Vacancy sensing is manual-ON, auto-OFF; occupancy is auto-ON, auto-OFF
Occupancy sensing only works with daylight

questions.explanation: Vacancy sensing requires a manual ON but turns lights off automatically; occupancy sensing does both automatically.

questions.prompt: How should daylight zones be oriented relative to a window wall?
questions.explanation: Zones parallel to the window wall let photocells dim only the fixtures receiving daylight.

questions.prompt: Which of these are recognized dimming methods? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 0-10V, DALI, and phase control are dimming methods. 'BACnet lumens' is not a dimming protocol.

questions.prompt: True or False: Finer control zoning generally increases both energy savings and device count.
questions.explanation: Finer zoning improves savings and flexibility but requires more devices and cost.

questions.prompt: Which four strategies form the core of most controls designs?

choices.text: Occupancy, daylight harvesting, scheduling, manual/task tuning

questions.explanation: The four core strategies are occupancy/vacancy sensing, daylight harvesting, scheduling, and manual/task tuning.
